bh.niti.100.m: Whether a task is good or bad, a wise person should first carefully weigh its outcome. The result of deeds done in great haste burns the heart like a thorn until one's dying day.
bh.niti.100.sa: गुणवदगुणवद्वा कुर्वता कार्यजातं परिणतिरवधार्या यत्नतः पण्डितेन । अतिरभसकृतानां कर्मणामाविपत्ते- र्भवति हृदयदाही शल्यतुल्यो विपाकः ॥

bh.niti.102.m: Let a man dive into the sea, climb to the peak of Meru, conquer his enemies in battle, learn trade, farming, service and every art and science, fly across the vast sky like a bird with all his effort: what is not to be will not happen, by the force of karma, and how can what is to be fail?
bh.niti.102.sa: मज्जत्वम्भसि यातु मेरुशिखरं शत्रून् जयत्वावहे वाणिज्यं कृषिसेवने च सकला विद्याः कलाः शिक्षताम् । आकाशं विपुलं प्रयातु खगवत्कृत्वा प्रयत्नं परं नाभाव्यं भवतीह कर्मवशतो भाव्यस्य नाशः कुतः ॥

bh.niti.105.m: Only here and there is the earth adorned by people poor in harsh words and rich in kind ones, content with their own spouses, who keep away from speaking ill of others.
bh.niti.105.sa: अप्रियवचनदरिद्रैः प्रियवचनाढ्यैः स्वदारपरितुष्टैः । परपरिवादनिवृत्तैः क्वचित्क्वचिन्मण्डिता वसुधा ॥

bh.niti.106.m: Even when harassed, the steadfast cannot be robbed of their steadiness. Hold a torch upside down: its flame never points downward.
roles: Gives dhairya as an inalienable quality.
bh.niti.106.sa: कदर्थितस्यापि हि धैर्यवृत्तेर्न शक्यते धैर्यगुणः प्रमार्ष्टुम् । अधोमुखस्यापि कृतस्य वह्नेर्नाधः शिखा याति कदाचिदेव ॥

bh.niti.14.m: Better to wander mountain passes with the creatures of the forest than to keep company with fools, even in the palace of Indra.
bh.niti.14.sa: वरं पर्वतदुर्गेषु भ्रान्तं वनचरैः सह । न मूर्खजनसम्पर्कः सुरेन्द्रभवनेष्वपि ॥

bh.niti.16.m: It never comes within a thief's sight; it always nourishes some deep good; given to those who ask, it grows greater; even at the end of an age it does not perish. Kings, drop your pride before those who own this inner wealth called learning. Who can compete with them?
bh.niti.16.sa: हर्तुर्याति न गोचरं किमपि शं पुष्णाति यत् सर्वदा- ऽप्यर्थिभ्यः प्रतिपाद्यमानमनिशं प्राप्नोति वृद्धिं पराम् । कल्पान्तेष्वपि न प्रयाति निधनं विद्याख्यमन्तर्धनं येषां तान् प्रति मानमुज्झत नृपाः कस्तैः सह स्पर्धते ॥

bh.niti.18.m: An angry Creator may destroy the swan's delight of roaming its lotus pond, but he cannot take away its famous skill of separating milk from water.
roles: Stand on what is still yours.
bh.niti.18.sa: अम्भोजिनीवनविहारविलासमेव हंसस्य हन्ति नितरां कुपितो विधाता । न त्वस्य दुग्धजलभेदविधौ प्रसिद्धां वैदग्ध्यकीर्तिमपहर्तुमसौ समर्थः ॥

bh.niti.19.m: Armlets do not adorn a person, nor necklaces bright as the moon, nor bathing, nor perfume, nor flowers, nor dressed hair. Speech alone, refined and well held, truly adorns a person. Ornaments wear away; the ornament of speech is the real ornament.
bh.niti.19.sa: केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषं हारा न चन्द्रोज्ज्वला न स्नानं न विलेपनं न कुसुमं नालङ्कृता मूर्धजाः । वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् ॥

bh.niti.20.m: Learning is a person's greater beauty, a hidden and guarded treasure. Learning brings enjoyment, fame and happiness; it is the teacher of teachers. In a foreign land learning is your kin; learning is the highest deity. Kings honour learning, not wealth. Without learning a person is little more than an animal.
bh.niti.20.sa: विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकं प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनं विद्या भोगकरी यशस्सुखकरी विद्या गुरूणां गुरुः । विद्या बन्धुजनो विदेशगमने विद्या परा देवता विद्या राजसु पूजिता न तु धनं विद्याविहीनः पशुः ॥

bh.niti.21.m: If you have forbearance, what need of armour? If you have anger, what need of enemies? If you have kinsmen, what need of fire? If a friend, what need of magic medicines? If the wicked are around, what need of snakes? If spotless learning, what need of riches? If modesty, what need of ornaments? If fine poetry, what need of a kingdom?
bh.niti.21.sa: क्षान्तिश्चेत् कवचेन किं किमरिभिः क्रोधोऽस्ति चेद्देहिनां ज्ञातिश्चेदनलेन किं यदि सुहृद् दिव्यौषधैः किं फलम् । किं सर्पैर्यदि दुर्जनाः किमु धनैर्विद्या न वन्द्या यदि व्रीडा चेत्किमु भूषणैः सुकविता यद्यस्ति राज्येन किम् ॥

bh.niti.23.m: Good company takes dullness from the mind, sprinkles truth into speech, raises one's dignity, removes wrongdoing, clears the heart and spreads one's good name in every direction. Tell me, what does good company not do for a person?
bh.niti.23.sa: जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति । चेतः प्रसादयति दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिं सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् ॥

bh.niti.25.m: A son of good conduct, a devoted and loving wife, a gracious master, an affectionate friend, kinsfolk who do not cheat, a mind without a trace of strain, a pleasing form, lasting prosperity, a face bright with learning: these come to the one with whom Hari, remover of the world's troubles, is pleased.
roles: Ordinary blessings are counted and received as grace.
bh.niti.25.sa: सूनुः सच्चरितः सती प्रियतमा स्वामी प्रसादोन्मुखः स्निग्धं मित्रमवञ्चकः परिजनो निष्क्लेशलेशं मनः । आकारो रुचिरः स्थिरश्च विभवो विद्यावदातं मुखं तुष्टे विष्टपकष्टहारिणि हरौ सम्प्राप्यते देहिना ॥

bh.niti.26.m: Refraining from taking life, restraint from seizing others' wealth, truthful speech, timely giving as one is able, silence in gossip about others' wives, breaking the current of craving, humility before elders, compassion for all beings: this is the common path to the good, unbroken in all the scriptures.
bh.niti.26.sa: प्राणाघातान्निवृत्तिः परधनहरणे संयमः सत्यवाक्यं काले शक्त्या प्रदानं युवतिजनकथामूकभावः परेषाम् । तृष्णास्रोतोविभङ्गो गुरुषु च विनयः सर्वभूतानुकम्पा सामान्यः सर्वशास्त्रेष्वनुपहतविधिः श्रेयसामेष पन्थाः ॥

bh.niti.27.m: The lowest do not begin at all, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin, but stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
bh.niti.27.sa: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ॥ विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति ॥

bh.niti.28.m: Do not ask the wicked for favours; do not ask a friend of slender means for money; love a just way of earning; do nothing base even when life is at stake; stand tall in trouble; follow in the footsteps of the great. Who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
roles: Shows the sword-edge vow of integrity.
bh.niti.28.sa: असन्तो नाभ्यर्थ्याः सुहृदपि न याच्यः कृशधनः प्रिया न्याय्या वृत्तिर्मलिनमसुभङ्गेऽप्यसुकरम् । विपद्युच्चैः स्थेयं पदमनुविधेयं च महतां सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥

bh.niti.3.m: An ignorant person is easily won over; an expert, more easily still. But a person puffed up by a scrap of knowledge not even Brahma, the Creator, can satisfy.
bh.niti.3.sa: अज्ञः सुखमाराध्यः सुखतरमाराध्यते विशेषज्ञः । ज्ञानलवदुर्विदग्धं ब्रह्मापि तं नरं न रञ्जयति ॥

bh.niti.31.m: The dog wags its tail, falls at the feet of whoever feeds it, rolls on the ground showing its mouth and belly; the lordly elephant looks on steadily and eats only after a hundred coaxing words.
bh.niti.31.sa: लाङ्गूलचालनमधश्चरणावपातं भूमौ निपत्य वदनोदरदर्शनं च । श्वा पिण्डदस्य कुरुते गजपुङ्गवस्तु धीरं विलोकयति चाटुशतैश्च भुङ्क्ते ॥

bh.niti.4.m: One might wrench a jewel from between a crocodile's teeth, swim an ocean tossing with rows of waves, wear an angry snake on one's head like a flower; but one cannot win over the mind of a fool who has dug in.
bh.niti.4.sa: प्रसह्य मणिमुद्धरेन्मकरवक्त्रदंष्ट्राङ्कुरा- त्समुद्रमपि संतरेत्प्रचलदूर्मिमालाकुलम् । भुजङ्गमपि कोपितं शिरसि पुष्पवद्धारये- न्न तु प्रतिनिविष्टमूर्खजनचित्तमाराधयेत् ॥

bh.niti.40.m: The same faculties, unimpaired; the same name; the same unclouded mind; the same speech. Yet a man deprived of the warmth of wealth becomes, in a moment, someone else. How strange!
bh.niti.40.sa: तानीन्द्रियाण्यविकलानि तदेव नाम सा बुद्धिरप्रतिहता वचनं तदेव । अर्थोष्मणा विरहितः पुरुषः क्षणेन सोऽप्यन्य एव भवतीति विचित्रमेतत् ॥

bh.niti.41.m: Whoever has wealth is well-born, learned, well-read and a judge of merit; he is the eloquent one, the handsome one. All virtues take shelter in gold.
roles: Shows seeing flattery for what it is.
bh.niti.41.sa: यस्यास्ति वित्तं स नरः कुलीनः स पण्डितः स श्रुतवान् गुणज्ञः । स एव वक्ता स च दर्शनीयः सर्वे गुणाः काञ्चनमाश्रयन्ति ॥

scene.s: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.

bh.niti.42.m: A king is ruined by bad counsel, an ascetic by attachment, a son by spoiling, a brahmin by neglecting study, a family by a wayward son, character by serving the wicked, modesty by drink, farming by neglect, affection by living far away, friendship by lack of warmth, prosperity by bad conduct, and wealth by careless spending.
bh.niti.42.sa: दौर्मन्त्र्यान्नृपतिर्विनश्यति यतिः सङ्गात् सुतो लालनाद् विप्रोऽनध्ययनात् कुलं कुतनयाच्छीलं खलोपासनात् । ह्रीर्मद्यादनवेक्षणादपि कृषिः स्नेहः प्रवासाश्र- यान्मैत्री चाप्रणयात् समृद्धिरनयात् त्यागः प्रमादाद्धनम् ॥

bh.niti.43.m: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
bh.niti.43.sa: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥

bh.niti.45.m: A man who has lost everything longs for a handful of barley; later, when full, he counts the whole earth as straw. Because nothing is fixed, a person's condition makes things look great or small.
roles: Shows less grip on any one valuation.
bh.niti.45.sa: परिक्षीणः कश्चित्स्पृहयति यवानां प्रसृतये स पश्चात् सम्पूर्णः कलयति धरित्रीं तृणसमाम् । अतश्चानैकान्त्याद्गुरुलघुतयाऽर्थेषु धनिना- मवस्था वस्तूनि प्रथयति च सङ्कोचयति च ॥

bh.niti.46.m: O king, if you wish to milk this cow, the earth, first nourish the people as one feeds the calf. When they are well and constantly cared for, the earth bears every kind of fruit, like a wish-granting vine.
bh.niti.46.sa: राजन् दुधुक्षसि यदि क्षितिधेनुमेतां तेनाद्य वत्समिव लोकममुं पुषाण । तस्मिंश्च सम्यगनिशं परिपोष्यमाणे नानाफलैः फलति कल्पलतेव भूमिः ॥

bh.niti.49.m: Whatever wealth, small or great, the Creator has written on your forehead, you will get it even in a desert, and no more even on Mount Meru. So be steady; do not play the beggar before the rich for nothing. Look: a pot draws the same water from a well as from the ocean.
roles: Shows one's measure is one's own.
bh.niti.49.sa: यद्धात्रा निजभालपट्टलिखितं स्तोकं महद्वा धनं तत् प्राप्नोति मरुस्थलेऽपि नितरां मेरौ ततो नाधिकम् । तद्धीरो भव वित्तवत्सु कृपणां वृत्तिं वृथा मा कृथाः कूपे पश्य पयोनिधावपि घटो गृह्णाति तुल्यं जलम् ॥

bh.niti.51.m: Friend chataka, listen carefully for a moment. Many clouds live in the sky, but not all are alike. Some drench the earth with rain; some only thunder for nothing. Do not speak pleading words before every cloud you see.
roles: Keeps asking for those who can and will help.
bh.niti.51.sa: रे रे चातक सावधानमनसा मित्र क्षणं श्रूयताम् अम्भोदा बहवो वसन्ति गगने सर्वेऽपि नैकादृशाः । केचिद्वृष्टिभिरार्द्रयन्ति धरणीं गर्जन्ति केचिद्वृथा यं यं पश्यसि तस्य तस्य पुरतो मा ब्रूहि दीनं वचः ॥

bh.niti.53.m: A wicked person should be avoided, even if adorned with learning. Is a snake any less frightening because it wears a jewel?
bh.niti.53.sa: दुर्जनः परिहर्तव्यो विद्ययालङ्कृतोऽपि सन् । मणिना भूषितः सर्पः किमसौ न भयङ्करः ॥

bh.niti.54.m: The modest are called dull; the devout, hypocrites; the pure, frauds; the brave, heartless; the thoughtful sage, a fool; the gentle speaker, servile; the spirited, arrogant; the eloquent, a chatterbox; the steady, weak. What virtue of the virtuous has the wicked not smeared?
bh.niti.54.sa: जाड्यं ह्रीमति गण्यते व्रतरुचौ दम्भः शुचौ कैतवं शूरे निर्घृणता मुनौ विमतिता दैन्यं प्रियालापिनि । तेजस्विन्यवलिप्तता मुखरता वक्तर्यशक्तिः स्थिरे तत्को नाम गुणो भवेत्स गुणिनां यो दुर्जनैर्नाङ्कितः ॥

bh.niti.55.m: If there is greed, what need of other faults? If backbiting, what need of other sins? If truth, what need of austerity? If a pure mind, what need of pilgrimage? If goodness of heart, what need of other virtues? If greatness, what need of ornaments? If true learning, what need of wealth? If disgrace, what need of death?
roles: Shows purity of mind as the real pilgrimage.
bh.niti.55.sa: लोभश्चेदगुणेन किं पिशुनता यद्यस्ति किं पातकैः सत्यं चेत्तपसा च किं शुचि मनो यद्यस्ति तीर्थेन किम् । सौजन्यं यदि किं गुणैः सुमहिमा यद्यस्ति किं मण्डनैः सद्विद्या यदि किं धनैरपयशो यद्यस्ति किं मृत्युना ॥

bh.niti.57.m: Rulers with fierce tempers have no one close to them. Fire burns even the priest who feeds it offerings.
roles: Shows for those near such a person even the one who serves gets burned.
bh.niti.57.sa: न कश्चिच्चण्डकोपानामात्मीयो नाम भूभुजाम् । होतारमपि जुह्वानं स्पृष्टो दहति पावकः ॥

bh.niti.58.m: Keep quiet and you are dumb; speak well and you are a babbler or a windbag; stay close and you are pushy; keep away and you lack confidence; be patient and you are a coward; refuse to put up with things and you are ill-bred. The duty of serving another is deep indeed, beyond the reach even of yogis.
roles: Depicts every choice turned into a fault.
bh.niti.58.sa: मौनान्मूकः प्रवचनपटुर्वातुलो जल्पको वा धृष्टः पार्श्वे वसति च सदा दूरतश्चाप्रगल्भः । क्षान्त्या भीरुर्यदि न सहते प्रायशो नाभिजातः सेवाधर्मः परमगहनो योगिनामप्यगम्यः ॥

bh.niti.60.m: Large at the start and shrinking bit by bit, or slight at first and growing afterwards: like the shade of a day's first and second halves is the friendship of the wicked and of the good.
roles: Slow friendships are the growing kind.
bh.niti.60.sa: आरम्भगुर्वी क्षयिणी क्रमेण लघ्वी पुरा वृद्धिमती च पश्चात् । दिनस्य पूर्वार्धपरार्धभिन्ना छायेव मैत्री खलसज्जनानाम् ॥

bh.niti.62.m: A longing for good company, delight in others' merits, humility before a teacher, a passion for learning, love for one's own wife, fear of public disgrace, devotion to Shiva, the strength to master oneself, freedom from bad company: I bow to the people in whom these pure qualities live.
bh.niti.62.sa: वाञ्छा सज्जनसङ्गमे परगुणे प्रीतिर्गुरौ नम्रता विद्यायां व्यसनं स्वयोषिति रतिर्लोकापवादाद्भयम् । भक्तिः शूलिनि शक्तिरात्मदमने संसर्गमुक्तिः खले येष्वेते निवसन्ति निर्मलगुणास्तेभ्यो नरेभ्यो नमः ॥

bh.niti.63.m: Steadiness in misfortune, forbearance in success, eloquence in the assembly, courage in battle, a love of good name, a passion for learning: these come naturally to great souls.
bh.niti.63.sa: विपदि धैर्यमथाभ्युदये क्षमा सदसि वाक्पटुता युधि विक्रमः । यशसि चाभिरुचिर्व्यसनं श्रुतौ प्रकृतिसिद्धमिदं हि महात्मनाम् ॥

bh.niti.64.m: Giving in secret, a warm welcome for whoever comes home, silence after doing a kindness, speaking in public of kindness received, no arrogance in wealth, talking of others without a whiff of contempt: who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
roles: Shows speaking openly of help received.
bh.niti.64.sa: प्रदानं प्रच्छन्नं गृहमुपगते सम्भ्रमविधिः प्रियं कृत्वा मौनं सदसि कथनं चाप्युपकृते । अनुत्सेको लक्ष्म्यामनभिभवगन्धाः परकथाः सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥

bh.niti.66.m: In prosperity the heart of the great becomes soft as a lotus; in adversity, hard as a mass of mountain rock.
bh.niti.66.sa: सम्पत्सु महतां चित्तं भवत्युत्पलकोमलम् । आपत्सु च महाशैलशिलासङ्घातकर्कशम् ॥

bh.niti.67.m: Water on red-hot iron leaves not even a name behind; the same water on a lotus leaf shines like a pearl; fallen into a sea oyster under the Svati star, it becomes a pearl. As a rule, low, middling or high qualities come from the company one keeps.
roles: Shows placing oneself deciding what one becomes.
bh.niti.67.sa: सन्तप्तायसि संस्थितस्य पयसो नामापि न ज्ञायते मुक्ताकारतया तदेव नलिनीपत्रस्थितं राजते । स्वात्यां सागरशुक्तिमध्यपतितं तन्मौक्तिकं जायते प्रायेणाधममध्यमोत्तमगुणः संसर्गतो जायते ॥

bh.niti.70.m: Rising by bowing low, making their own virtues known by speaking of others', achieving their own aims by working hard for others, shaming slanderers whose mouths are full of harsh words simply by their patience: the good, whose conduct is a wonder, are honoured in the world. Who would not revere them?
roles: Patience as the answer to slander.
bh.niti.70.sa: नम्रत्वेनोन्नमन्तः परगुणकथनैः स्वान् गुणान् ख्यापयन्तः स्वार्थान् सम्पादयन्तो विततपृथुतरारम्भयत्नाः परार्थे । क्षान्त्यैवाक्षेपरुक्षाक्षरमुखरमुखान् दुर्जनान् दूषयन्तः सन्तः साश्चर्यचर्या जगति बहुमताः कस्य नाभ्यर्चनीयाः ॥

bh.niti.71.m: Trees bow low with fruit; clouds hang low with new rain; the good are not puffed up by prosperity. This is the very nature of those who help others.
roles: Shows those who exist to give.
bh.niti.71.sa: भवन्ति नम्रास्तरवः फलोद्गमै- र्नवाम्बुभिर्दूरविलम्बिनो घनाः । अनुद्धताः सत्पुरुषाः समृद्धिभिः स्वभाव एवैष परोपकारिणाम् ॥

bh.niti.72.m: The ear is beautiful through learning, not earrings; the hand through giving, not bracelets; the body of the compassionate shines through helping others, not through sandal paste.
bh.niti.72.sa: श्रोत्रं श्रुतेनैव न कुण्डलेन दानेन पाणिर्न तु कङ्कणेन । विभाति कायः करुणापराणां परोपकारैर्न तु चन्दनेन ॥

bh.niti.73.m: He keeps you from wrong and steers you to what is good; he guards your secrets and makes your good qualities known; he does not leave you in trouble and gives when it is needed. The good call these the marks of a true friend.
roles: Names a checklist for being a friend.
bh.niti.73.sa: पापान्निवारयति योजयते हिताय गुह्यं निगूहति गुणान् प्रकटीकरोति । आपद्गतं च न जहाति ददाति काले सन्मित्रलक्षणमिदं निगदन्ति सन्तः ॥

bh.niti.75.m: Good people serve others' interests, setting their own aside. Ordinary people work for others so long as it does not clash with their own interest. Those who wreck others' good for their own gain are demons in human form. But those who wreck others' good for no gain at all: what to call them, we do not know.
bh.niti.75.sa: एते सत्पुरुषाः परार्थघटकाः स्वार्थं परित्यज्य ये सामान्यास्तु परार्थमुद्यमभृतः स्वार्थाविरोधेन ये । तेऽमी मानवराक्षसाः परहितं स्वार्थाय विघ्नन्ति ये ये विघ्नन्ति निरर्थकं परहितं ते के न जानीमहे ॥

bh.niti.76.m: Milk gave all its qualities to the water that joined it. Seeing the milk being heated, the water offered itself into the fire. Seeing its friend in danger, the milk rose up to follow it into the fire, and settled only when joined with water again. Such is the friendship of the good.
roles: Gives milk and water returning qualities.
bh.niti.76.sa: क्षीरेणात्मगतोदकाय हि गुणा दत्ताः पुरा तेऽखिलाः क्षीरोत्तापमवेक्ष्य तेन पयसा स्वात्मा कृशाणौ हुतः । गन्तुं पावकमुन्मनस्तदभवद् दृष्ट्वा तु मित्रापदं युक्तं तेन जलेन शाम्यति सतां मैत्री पुनस्त्वीदृशी ॥

bh.niti.78.m: Cut off craving, practise forbearance, give up arrogance, take no delight in wrong, speak the truth, follow the path of the good, serve the wise, honour those worthy of honour, win over even your enemies, show courtesy, guard your good name, be kind to those in pain: this is how the good behave.
roles: Cultivates kindness to those in pain.
bh.niti.78.sa: तृष्णां छिन्धि भज क्षमां जहि मदं पापे रतिं मा कृथाः सत्यं ब्रूह्यनुयाहि साधुपदवीं सेवस्व विद्वज्जनम् । मान्यान् मानय विद्विषोऽप्यनुनय प्रख्यापय प्रश्रयं कीर्तिं पालय दुःखिते कुरु दयामेतत् सतां चेष्टितम् ॥

bh.niti.79.m: Full of the nectar of goodness in mind, speech and body, delighting the three worlds with a stream of kindnesses, always turning the tiniest atom of merit in others into a mountain and blossoming in their own hearts: how many such good people are there?
bh.niti.79.sa: मनसि वचसि काये पुण्यपीयूषपूर्णाः त्रिभुवनमुपकारश्रेणिभिः प्रीणयन्तः । परगुणपरमाणून् पर्वतीकृत्य नित्यं निजहृदि विकसन्तः सन्ति सन्तः कियन्तः ॥

bh.niti.8.m: When I knew a little, I was blind with pride like an elephant in rut, and my mind swelled: 'I know everything.' When, little by little, I learned from the wise, I realised 'I am a fool', and my pride left me like a fever.
roles: Shows learning little by little from those who know.
bh.niti.8.sa: यदा किञ्चिज्ज्ञोऽहं गज इव मदान्धः समभवम् तदा सर्वज्ञोऽस्मीत्यभवदवलिप्तं मम मनः । यदा किञ्चित्किञ्चिद्बुधजनसकाशादवगतम् तदा मूर्खोऽस्मीति ज्वर इव मदो मे व्यपगतः ॥

bh.niti.81.m: The gods were not satisfied by priceless jewels, nor frightened off by the terrible poison; they did not rest until they had the nectar. The steadfast do not stop short of what they have set out to do.
roles: Shows neither lesser prizes nor poison ends the effort.
bh.niti.81.sa: रत्नैर्महार्हैस्तुतुषुर्न देवा न भेजिरे भीमविषेण भीतिम् । सुधां विना न प्रययुर्विरामं न निश्चितार्थाद्विरमन्ति धीराः ॥

bh.niti.82.m: Sometimes he sleeps on the ground, sometimes on a couch; sometimes he lives on greens, sometimes on fine rice; sometimes he wears rags, sometimes heavenly garments. A person of spirit set on a purpose counts neither hardship nor comfort.
roles: Shows indifference to conditions while working.
bh.niti.82.sa: क्वचित् पृथ्वीशय्यः क्वचिदपि च पर्यङ्कशयनः क्वचिच्छाकाहारः क्वचिदपि च शाल्योदनरुचिः । क्वचित् कण्ठाधारी क्वचिदपि च दिव्याम्बरधरो मनस्वी कार्यार्थी न गणयति च दुःखं न च सुखम् ॥

bh.niti.83.m: Courtesy is the ornament of power; restraint in speech, of valour; calm, of knowledge; humility, of learning; giving to the deserving, of wealth; freedom from anger, of austerity; forbearance, of those in authority; sincerity, of dharma. But character, the root of all these, is the highest ornament.
roles: Shows forbearance is named as the ornament of the one who has power.
bh.niti.83.sa: ऐश्वर्यस्य विभूषणं सुजनता शौर्यस्य वाक्संयमो ज्ञानस्योपशमः श्रुतस्य विनयो वित्तस्य पात्रे व्ययः । अक्रोधस्तपसः क्षमा प्रभवितुर्धर्मस्य निर्व्याजता सर्वेषामपि सर्वकारणमिदं शीलं परं भूषणम् ॥

bh.niti.84.m: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
bh.niti.84.sa: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥

bh.niti.85.m: A ball struck down by the hand flies right back up. As a rule, the misfortunes of those who live rightly do not last.
bh.niti.85.sa: पातितोऽपि कराघातैरुत्पतत्येव कन्दुकः । प्रायेण साधुवृत्तनामस्थायिन्यो विपत्तयः ॥

bh.niti.86.m: Laziness is the great enemy that lives in a person's own body. There is no friend like effort; one who works does not sink.
bh.niti.86.sa: आलस्यं हि मनुष्याणां शरीरस्थो महारिपुः । नास्त्युद्यमसमो बन्धुः कुर्वाणो नावसीदति ॥

bh.niti.87.m: A tree that is cut grows again; the waning moon waxes again in the world. Reflecting on this, the good are not tormented in this world.
roles: Draws patience from the tree and the moon.
bh.niti.87.sa: छिन्नोऽपि रोहति तरुश्चन्द्रः क्षीणोऽपि वर्धते लोके । इति विमृशन्तः सन्तः सन्तप्यन्ते न लोकेऽस्मिन् ॥

bh.niti.90.m: The fruit a person reaps depends on past actions, and even the mind follows one's actions. Even so, a wise person should act only after careful thought.
bh.niti.90.sa: कर्मायत्तं फलं पुंसां बुद्धिः कर्मानुसारिणी । तथापि सुधिया भाव्यं सुविचार्यैव कुर्वता ॥

bh.niti.93.m: The Creator fashions a jewel of a person, a mine of every virtue, an ornament to the earth, and then, if he makes him perish in a moment, alas! what folly in the Creator!
roles: Shows open protest at the unfairness of it.
bh.niti.93.sa: सृजति तावदशेषगुणाकरं पुरुषरत्नमलङ्करणं भुवः । तदपि तत्क्षणभङ्गि करोति चेदहह कष्टमपण्डितता विधेः ॥

bh.niti.95.m: We bow to the gods, but they are under fate's control. Fate deserves worship, but it only gives the fruit of fixed actions. If the fruit depends on action, what of the gods, what of fate? Salutations to actions themselves, over which even fate has no power.
roles: Names effort as where agency lies.
bh.niti.95.sa: नमस्यामो देवान्ननु हतविधेस्तेऽपि वशगा विधिर्वन्द्यः सोऽपि प्रतिनियतकर्मैकफलदः । फलं कर्मायत्तं यदि किममरैः किञ्च विधिना नमस्तत्कर्मभ्यो विधिरपि न येभ्यः प्रभवति ॥

bh.vairagya.10.m: There is a river called Hope. Its water is wishes, its waves are craving; passions are its crocodiles, doubts its birds; it uproots the trees of courage; its whirlpools of delusion are hard to cross and deep, and its banks of worry tower high. Only great yogis, pure in mind, who reach the far shore, rejoice.
bh.vairagya.10.sa: आशा नाम नदी मनोरथजला तृष्णातरङ्गाकुला रागग्राहवती वितर्कविहगा धैर्यद्रुमध्वंसिनी । मोहावर्तसुदुस्तरातिगहना प्रोत्तुङ्गचिन्तातटी तस्याः पारगता विशुद्धमनसो नन्दन्ति योगीश्वराः ॥

bh.vairagya.12.m: Pleasures will certainly leave, however long they stay with us. Then what difference is there in parting? Only that people do not let them go themselves. Leaving of their own accord, they bring the mind unequalled torment; given up by oneself, they bring endless peace.
bh.vairagya.12.sa: अवश्यं यातारश्चिरतरमुषित्वापि विषया वियोगे को भेदस्त्यजति न जनो यत्स्वयममून् । व्रजन्तः स्वातन्त्र्यादतुलपरितापाय मनसः स्वयं त्यक्ता ह्येते शमसुखमनन्तं विदधति ॥

bh.vairagya.18.m: Let the moth fall into the blazing flame not knowing that it burns; let the fish swallow the bait not knowing the hook. But we, knowing full well, still do not let go of desires tangled in a net of dangers. Ah, how deep is the power of delusion!
bh.vairagya.18.sa: अजानन्दाहात्म्यं पततु शलभस्तीव्रदहने स मीनोऽप्यज्ञानाद्वडिशयुतमश्नातु पिशितम् । विजानन्तोऽप्येते वयमिह विपज्जालजटिलान् न मुञ्चामः कामानहह गहनो मोहमहिमा ॥

bh.vairagya.19.m: When the mouth dries with thirst, one drinks cool sweet water; pained by hunger, one gobbles rice with meat and the rest; when the fire of desire flares, one holds a woman close. People mistake the cure of a disease for happiness.
bh.vairagya.19.sa: तृषा शुष्यत्यास्ये पिबति सलिलं शीतमधुरं क्षुधार्तः शाल्यान्नं कवलयति मांसादिकलितम् । प्रदीप्ते कामाग्नौ सुदृढतरमालिङ्गति वधूं प्रतीकारं व्याधेः सुखमिति विपर्यस्यति जनः ॥

bh.vairagya.21.m: If he did not have to see his wife, wretched, her worn clothes tugged by little children with pinched faces crying with hunger, the household without food, what self-respecting man would say 'give', his throat choking with fear of refusal and his words breaking and fading, for the sake of his own wretched belly?
roles: The choking voice of someone forced to ask.
bh.vairagya.21.sa: दीना दीनमुखैः सदैव शिशुकैराकृष्टजीर्णाम्बरा क्रोशद्भिः क्षुधितैर्निरन्नविधुरा दृश्या न चेद्गेहिनी । याञ्चाभङ्गभयेन गद्गदगलत्त्रुट्यद्विलीनाक्षरं को देहीति वदेत्स्वदग्धजठरस्यार्थे मनस्वी पुमान् ॥

bh.vairagya.29.m: Those always delighted by contentment have joy that is undivided; the others, minds crowded with greed for money, never kill their craving. So for whom did fate make wealth, and what kind of place is it? Mount Meru, whose golden glory ends in itself, does not appeal to me.
roles: Shows joy already whole in the contented.
bh.vairagya.29.sa: ये सन्तोषनिरन्तरप्रमुदितास्तेषां न भिन्ना मुदो ये त्वन्ये धनलुब्धसंकुलधियस्तेषां न तृष्णा हता । इत्थं कस्य कृते कृतः स विधिना कीदृक्पदं सम्पदां स्वात्मन्येव समाप्तहेममहिमा मेरुर्न मे रोचते ॥

bh.vairagya.3.m: I dug up the earth hoping for treasure, smelted the ores of mountains, crossed the ocean, lord of rivers, worked hard to please kings, spent nights in cremation grounds with my mind fixed on mantras, and I did not get even a broken cowrie. Craving, be satisfied now!
bh.vairagya.3.sa: उत्खातं निधिशङ्कया क्षितितलं ध्माता गिरेर्धातवो निस्तीर्णः सरितां पतिर्नृपतयो यत्नेन संतोषिताः । मन्त्राराधनतत्परेण मनसा नीताः श्मशाने निशाः प्राप्तः काणवराटकोऽपि न मया तृष्णे सकामा भव ॥

bh.vairagya.31.m: In pleasure lies the fear of disease; in high birth, the fear of a fall; in wealth, fear of the king; in honour, fear of humiliation; in strength, fear of enemies; in beauty, fear of old age; in learning, fear of rival debaters; in virtue, fear of the wicked; in the body, fear of death. Everything in this world carries fear; only dispassion is fearless.
bh.vairagya.31.sa: भोगे रोगभयं कुले च्युतिभयं वित्ते नृपालाद्भयं माने दैन्यभयं बले रिपुभयं रूपे जराया भयम् । शास्त्रे वादिभयं गुणे खलभयं काये कृतान्ताद्भयं सर्वं वस्तु भयान्वितं भुवि नृणां वैराग्यमेवाभयम् ॥

bh.vairagya.33.m: Health is uprooted by hundreds of worries and illnesses of every kind; where fortune arrives, disasters rush in after it as though through open doors; death quickly and helplessly makes everything born its own. What has this unchecked fate made that is stable?
roles: Shows seeing instability as the rule.
bh.vairagya.33.sa: आधिव्याधिशतैर्जनस्य विविधैरारोग्यमुन्मूल्यते लक्ष्मीर्यत्र पतन्ति तत्र विवृतद्वारा इव व्यापदः । जातं जातमवश्यमाशु विवशं मृत्युः करोत्यात्मसात् तत्किं तेन निरङ्कुशेन विधिना यन्निर्मितं सुस्थिरम् ॥

bh.vairagya.35.m: Pleasures flicker like lightning playing in a canopy of clouds; life is as fragile as water clinging to wind-tossed lotus leaves; the longings of youth are fickle. Knowing this, wise ones, quickly set your minds on yoga, which steadiness and stillness make easy to attain.
roles: Steadiness and stillness make yoga reachable.
bh.vairagya.35.sa: भोगा मेघवितानमध्यविलसत्सौदामिनीचञ्चला आयुर्वायुविघट्टिताब्जपटलीलीनाम्बुवद्भङ्गुरम् । लोला यौवनलालसास्तनुभृतामित्याकलय्य द्रुतं योगे धैर्यसमाधिसिद्धसुलभे बुद्धिं विधध्वं बुधाः ॥

bh.vairagya.36.m: Life is restless as a wave; the glow of youth lasts a few days; wealth is as fleeting as a thought; pleasures flash like monsoon lightning; even the embrace of loved ones round the neck does not last long. Set your mind on Brahman to cross the ocean of worldly fear.
roles: Shows Brahman as the one thing to hold.
bh.vairagya.36.sa: आयुः कल्लोललोलं कतिपयदिवसस्थायिनी यौवनश्रीः अर्थाः संकल्पकल्पा घनसमयतडिद्विभ्रमा भोगपूगाः । कण्ठाश्लेषोपगूढं तदपि च न चिरं यत्प्रियाभिः प्रणीतं ब्रह्मण्यासक्तचित्ता भवत भवभयाम्बोधिपारं तरीतुम् ॥

bh.vairagya.38.m: Old age crouches like a tigress, snarling; diseases strike the body like enemies; life leaks away like water from a cracked pot; and still people do harm. How strange!
roles: Shows time is short for doing what is unwholesome.
bh.vairagya.38.sa: व्याघ्रीव तिष्ठति जरा परितर्जयन्ती रोगाश्च शत्रव इव प्रहरन्ति देहम् । आयुः परिस्रवति भिन्नघटादिवाम्भो लोकस्तथाप्यहितमाचरतीति चित्रम् ॥

bh.vairagya.4.m: I somehow put up with the taunts of the wicked while trying to please them; I held back my tears and laughed with an empty heart; I folded my hands even before people whose minds were numbed by money. Hope, futile hope, how much more will you make me dance?
roles: Shows folding hands before people numbed by money.
bh.vairagya.4.sa: खलालापाः सोढाः कथमपि तदाराधनपरैः निगृह्यान्तर्बाष्पं हसितमपि शून्येन मनसा । कृतो वित्तस्तम्भप्रतिहतधियामञ्जलिरपि त्वमाशे मोघाशे किमपरमतो नर्तयसि माम् ॥

bh.vairagya.41.m: That lovely city, that great king, that circle of vassals at his side, that learned court, those moon-faced women, that proud crowd of princes, those bards and their tales: all of it has passed into memory by Time's power. Salutations to that Time.
roles: Shows loss met with a salutation.
bh.vairagya.41.sa: सा रम्या नगरी महान्स नृपतिः सामन्तचक्रं च तत् पार्श्वे तस्य च सा विदग्धपरिषत्ताश्चन्द्रबिम्बाननाः । उद्वृत्तः स च राजपुत्रनिवहस्ते बन्दिनस्ताः कथाः सर्वं यस्य वशादगात्स्मृतिपथं कालाय तस्मै नमः ॥

bh.vairagya.42.m: Where there were many in a house, one remains; where there was one, many come, and in the end not even one. So Time, rolling night and day like a pair of dice, plays on the board of the world with living beings as its pieces.
roles: Shows coming and going as Time's play.
bh.vairagya.42.sa: यत्रानेकः क्वचिदपि गृहे तत्र तिष्ठत्यथैको यत्राप्येकस्तदनु बहवस्तत्र नैकोऽपि चान्ते । इत्थं नेयौ रजनिदिवसौ लोलयन्द्वाविवाक्षौ कालः कल्यो भुवनफलके क्रीडति प्राणिशारैः ॥

bh.vairagya.43.m: With the sun's coming and going, life shrinks day by day; with business heavy with many tasks, we do not notice time passing; seeing birth, age, misfortune and death, we feel no alarm. The world has drunk the wine of heedlessness and gone mad.
bh.vairagya.43.sa: आदित्यस्य गतागतैरहरहः संक्षीयते जीवितं व्यापारैर्बहुकार्यभारगुरुभिः कालोऽपि न ज्ञायते । दृष्ट्वा जन्मजराविपत्तिमरणं त्रासश्च नोत्पद्यते पीत्वा मोहमयीं प्रमादमदिरामुन्मत्तभूतं जगत् ॥

bh.vairagya.44.m: Thinking 'it is the same night again, the same day', creatures run about in vain, busy as ever with the tasks they have set going; with work full of the same repeated things, tormented by this round of existence, alas, out of delusion we feel no shame.
roles: Names the sameness of days, said from inside.
bh.vairagya.44.sa: रात्रिः सैव पुनः स एव दिवसो मत्वा मुधा जन्तवो धावन्त्युद्यमिनस्तथैव निभृतप्रारब्धतत्तत्क्रियाः । व्यापारैः पुनरुक्तभूत विषयैरित्थंविधेनामुना संसारेण कदर्थिता वयमहो मोहान्न लज्जामहे ॥

bh.vairagya.47.m: I did not gain spotless learning, nor earn wealth; I did not even serve my parents with an attentive mind; I did not hold wide-eyed beloveds even in dreams. Time is driven on, like a crow greedy for others' scraps.
roles: Shows a reckoning of what was not done in first person.
bh.vairagya.47.sa: विद्या नाधिगता कलङ्करहिता वित्तं च नोपार्जितं शुश्रूषापि समाहितेन मनसा पित्रोर्न सम्पादिता । आलोलायतलोचनाः प्रियतमाः स्वप्नेऽपि नालिङ्गिताः कालोऽयं परपिण्डलोलुपतया काकैरिव प्रेर्यते ॥

bh.vairagya.48.m: Those who gave us birth are long gone into memory; those with whom we grew up have also passed into memory; and now we, nearer to falling each day, have come to the state of trees on a sandy riverbank.
roles: Shows nearer to falling each day.
bh.vairagya.48.sa: वयं येभ्यो जाताश्चिरपरिचिता एव खलु ते समं यैः संवृद्धाः स्मृतिविषयतां तेऽपि गमिताः । इदानीमेते स्मः प्रतिदिवसमासन्नपतना गतास्तुल्यावस्थां सिकतिलनदीतीरतरुभिः ॥

bh.vairagya.49.m: A human life is measured at a hundred years. Half goes in night; of the other half, half again goes in childhood and old age; the rest is spent in sickness, separation and sorrow, in serving others. In a life more restless than a wave, where is happiness for any creature?
bh.vairagya.49.sa: आयुर्वर्षशतं नृणां परिमितं रात्रौ तदर्धं गतं तस्यार्धस्य परस्य चार्धमपरं बालत्ववृद्धत्वयोः । शेषं व्याधिवियोगदुःखसहितं सेवादिभिर्नीयते जीवे वारितरङ्गचञ्चलतरे सौख्यं कुतः प्राणिनाम् ॥

bh.vairagya.50.m: For a moment a child, for a moment a youth in love, for a moment penniless, for a moment wealthy; then, limbs worn by age and body painted with wrinkles like an actor, man exits behind the curtain of Death at the end of the play.
roles: Treats poor and rich as both scenes.
bh.vairagya.50.sa: क्षणं बालो भूत्वा क्षणमपि युवा कामरसिकः क्षणं वित्तैर्हीनः क्षणमपि च सम्पूर्णविभवः । जराजीर्णैरङ्गैर्नट इव वलीमण्डिततनुः नरः संसारान्ते विशति यमधानीयवनिकाम् ॥

bh.vairagya.51.m: You are a king; we too stand tall with the pride of wisdom gained from serving our teachers. You are famous for your wealth; poets spread our fame in every direction. So the gap between us in honour and riches is not wide. If you turn your face from us, we too are entirely indifferent.
roles: Shows wanting nothing from the one who withholds.
bh.vairagya.51.sa: त्वं राजा वयमप्युपासितगुरुप्रज्ञाभिमानोन्नताः ख्यातस्त्वं विभवैर्यशांसि कवयो दिक्षु प्रतन्वन्ति नः । इत्थं मानधनातिदूरमुभयोरप्यावयोरन्तरं यद्यस्मासु पराङ्मुखोऽसि वयमप्येकान्ततो निःस्पृहाः ॥

bh.vairagya.53.m: We are content here with bark garments, you with silk; the contentment is equal, and the difference makes no difference. He is poor whose craving is vast. When the mind is content, who is rich and who is poor?
bh.vairagya.53.sa: वयमिह परितुष्टा वल्कलैस्त्वं दुकूलैः सम इव परितोषो निर्विशेषो विशेषः । स तु भवतु दरिद्रो यस्य तृष्णा विशाला मनसि च परितुष्टे कोऽर्थवान्को दरिद्रः ॥

bh.vairagya.57.m: Great-hearted lords created this world long ago; others held it; others conquered it and gave it away like straw; and even now other heroes enjoy all fourteen worlds. What is this fever of pride in men over lordship of a few towns?
bh.vairagya.57.sa: विपुलहृदयैरीशैरेतज्जगज्जनितं पुरा विधृतमपरैर्दत्तं चान्यैर्विजित्य तृणं यथा । इह हि भुवनान्यन्ये धीराश्चतुर्दश भुञ्जते कतिपयपुरस्वाम्ये पुंसां क एष मदज्वरः ॥

bh.vairagya.6.m: We forgave, but not out of forgiveness; we gave up home comforts, but not out of contentment; we bore unbearable cold, wind and heat, but not as austerity; we thought of money day and night with held breath, not of Shiva's feet. We did every act the sages did, and were cheated of every one of their fruits.
roles: Shows looking back on effort spent for the wrong end.
bh.vairagya.6.sa: क्षान्तं न क्षमया गृहोचितसुखं त्यक्तं न संतोषतः सोढा दुःसहशीतवाततपनक्लेशा न तप्तं तपः । ध्यातं वित्तमहर्निशं नियमितप्राणैर्न शम्भोः पदं तत्तत्कर्म कृतं यदेव मुनिभिस्तैस्तैः फलैर्वञ्चिताः ॥

bh.vairagya.61.m: O heart, why do you enter into weariness, day after day trying to please the minds of others in so many ways, to win their favour? When you are at peace within, your own clear resolve rises by itself like a cluster of wish-granting gems: what wish of yours would it not fulfil?
roles: Names a heart settled within as its own wish-granting gem.
bh.vairagya.61.sa: परेषां चेतांसि प्रतिदिवसमाराध्य बहुधा प्रसादं किं नेतुं विशसि हृदय क्लेशकलितम् । प्रसन्ने त्वय्यन्तः स्वयमुदितचिन्तामणिगणो विविक्तः संकल्पः किमभिलषितं पुष्यति न ते ॥

bh.vairagya.62.m: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
bh.vairagya.62.sa: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥

bh.vairagya.67.m: You gained fortunes that fulfil every desire: so what? You set your foot on your enemies' heads: so what? You won over friends with your riches: so what? Bodies lasted an aeon: so what?
roles: Opens the question of what would be enough.
bh.vairagya.67.sa: प्राप्ताः श्रियः सकलकामदुघास्ततः किं न्यस्तं पदं शिरसि विद्विषतां ततः किम् । सम्पादिताः प्रणयिनो विभवैस्ततः किं कल्पस्थितास्तनुभृतां तनवस्ततः किम् ॥

bh.vairagya.7.m: We did not enjoy pleasures; pleasures consumed us. We did not perform austerity; we were scorched. Time did not pass; we passed. Craving did not grow old; we grew old.
roles: Depicts a life used up by its own wants.
bh.vairagya.7.sa: भोगा न भुक्ता वयमेव भुक्ताः तपो न तप्तं वयमेव तप्ताः । कालो न यातो वयमेव याता- स्तृष्णा न जीर्णा वयमेव जीर्णाः ॥

bh.vairagya.70.m: You plunge into the underworld, leap across the sky, wander round every direction, O mind, out of restlessness. Why do you never, even by mistake, remember that pure Brahman, your own Self, by which you would find peace?
roles: Shows Brahman as one's own self.
bh.vairagya.70.sa: पातालमाविशसि यासि नभो विलङ्घ्य दिङ्मण्डलं भ्रमसि मानस चापलेन । भ्रान्त्यापि जातु विमलं कथमात्मनीनं न ब्रह्म संस्मरसि निर्वृतिमेषि येन ॥

bh.vairagya.71.m: What use are the Vedas, the smritis, reading the Puranas, the vast shastras, and the confusions of ritual that earn a hut in the village of heaven? Apart from the one thing, entry into the bliss of the Self, the fire that burns away the whole burden of worldly sorrow, the rest is merchants' trading.
bh.vairagya.71.sa: किं वेदैः स्मृतिभिः पुराणपठनैः शास्त्रैर्महाविस्तरैः स्वर्गग्रामकुटीनिवासफलदैः कर्मक्रियाविभ्रमैः । मुक्त्वैकं भवदुःखभाररचनाविध्वंसकालानलं स्वात्मानन्दपदप्रवेशकलनं शेषैर्वणिग्वृत्तिभिः ॥

scene.s: Weighing what lasts: religion without inner peace is trading; old age can bring neglect; act while healthy, not when the house is on fire. The poet admits not knowing how to spend a short life.
scene.t: Vairagyashatakam: Weighing the lasting and the passing

bh.vairagya.75.m: While this body is healthy and free of illness, while old age is far off, while the senses are unimpaired and life has not run down, the wise should make a great effort for their own highest good. Once the house is on fire, what use is digging a well?
roles: Names the great effort beginning now.
bh.vairagya.75.sa: यावत्स्वस्थमिदं शरीरमरुजं यावज्जरा दूरतो यावच्चेन्द्रियशक्तिरप्रतिहता यावत्क्षयो नायुषः । आत्मश्रेयसि तावदेव विदुषा कार्यः प्रयत्नो महान् संदीप्ते भवने तु कूपखननं प्रत्युद्यमः कीदृशः ॥

bh.vairagya.76.m: Shall we live as ascetics beside the heavenly river? Or courteously serve our wives, generous in virtue? Or drink the floods of scripture, or the nectar of many kinds of poetry? We do not know what to do, in a human life that lasts a few blinks.
roles: Names each path has a claim.
bh.vairagya.76.sa: तपस्यन्तः सन्तः किमधिनिवसामः सुरनदीं गुणोदारान्दारानुत परिचरामः सविनयम् । पिबामः शास्त्रौघानुत विविधकाव्यामृतरसान् न विद्मः किं कुर्मः कतिपयनिमेषायुषि जने ॥

bh.vairagya.8.m: The face is overrun by wrinkles, the head marked with grey, the limbs grow slack; craving alone grows young.
roles: Shows wanting that gets younger as the body gets older.
bh.vairagya.8.sa: वलीभिर्मुखमाक्रान्तं पलितेनाङ्कितं शिरः । गात्राणि शिथिलायन्ते तृष्णैका तरुणायते ॥

bh.vairagya.82.m: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
bh.vairagya.82.sa: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥

bh.vairagya.84.m: Between Maheshvara, lord of the worlds, and Janardana, the inner Self of the world, I see no difference in essence; still, my devotion goes to the one who wears the young moon on his head.
roles: Shows no quarrel between forms of God.
bh.vairagya.84.sa: महेश्वरे वा जगतामधीश्वरे जनार्दने वा जगदन्तरात्मनि । न वस्तुभेदप्रतिपत्तिरस्ति मे तथापि भक्तिस्तरुणेन्दुशेखरे ॥

bh.vairagya.9.m: The wish for pleasures has gone; the respect people paid us has melted away; our peers have gone to heaven, and friends dear as life are quickly following; we rise slowly with a stick, our eyes clouded with darkness; and still, foolish body, it startles at the approach of death!
roles: Depicts fear of death that outlasts every reason to stay.
bh.vairagya.9.sa: निवृत्ता भोगेच्छा पुरुषबहुमानोऽपि गलितः समानाः स्वर्याताः सपदि सुहृदो जीवितसमाः । शनैर्यष्ट्युत्थानं घनतिमिररुद्धे च नयने अहो मूढः कायस्तदपि मरणापायचकितः ॥

bh.vairagya.92.m: For the high-minded the whole universe is a mere ring; what is there in it to be greedy for? The ocean is not churned up by the flicker of a little fish.
roles: Names depth that is not disturbed.
bh.vairagya.92.sa: ब्रह्माण्डं मण्डलीमात्रं किं लोभाय मनस्विनः । शफरीस्फुरितेनाब्धिः क्षुब्धो न खलु जायते ॥

bh.vairagya.94.m: The earth is his great bed, his arm a broad pillow, the sky his canopy, the friendly breeze his fan, the autumn moon his lamp; delighted in the company of his bride, Renunciation, the sage sleeps happy and calm, rich beyond measure, like a king.
roles: Shows complete ease with nothing owned.
bh.vairagya.94.sa: महाशय्या पृथ्वी विपुलमुपधानं भुजलता वितानं चाकाशं व्यजनमनुकूलोऽयमनिलः । शरच्चन्द्रो दीपो विरतिवनितासङ्गमुदितः सुखी शान्तः शेते मुनिरतनुभूतिर्नृप इव ॥

bh.vairagya.96.m: 'Is this a chandala? A twice-born? A shudra, or an ascetic? Or some great yogi with a mind skilled in discerning truth?' Talked about like this by people noisy with doubts and chatter, the yogis go their own way, neither angry nor pleased.
roles: Neither angered nor flattered, remaining equanimous.
bh.vairagya.96.sa: चण्डालः किमयं द्विजातिरथवा शूद्रोऽथ किं तापसः किं वा तत्त्वविवेकपेशलमतिर्योगीश्वरः कोऽपि किम् । इत्युत्पन्नविकल्पजल्पमुखरैराभाष्यमाणा जनैः न क्रुद्धाः पथि नैव तुष्टमनसो यान्ति स्वयं योगिनः ॥

scene.s: Portraits of the wandering sage: unbothered when people argue over his caste, sleeping under the sky like a king, and finally bidding farewell to the five elements.
scene.t: Vairagyashatakam: The way of the free ascetic

kabir.kk.66.m: The lily lives in the water and the moon lives in the sky; yet whoever is dear to someone is always near them.
roles: Trusts in a bond that space does not cut.
kabir.kk.66.sa: जल में बसै कमोदिनी चन्दा बसै अकास। जो है जाको भावता सो ताही के पास॥

kabir.kk.71.m: Father, forgive my faults, you who lift up the poor. Even if I am a bad son, I am still my father's to look after.
roles: Asking forgiveness as a child asks.
kabir.kk.71.sa: अवगुन मेरे बाप जो बकसु गरीब निवाज। जो मैं पूत कपूत हौं तऊ पिता को लाज॥

kabir.sdg.samrathai.1.m: Whoever has no one has you; whoever has you has everyone. Master, at your court no one goes away empty-handed.
roles: Shows going to the one open door.
kabir.sdg.samrathai.1.sa: जिसहि न कोई तिसहि तू, जिस तू तिस सब कोइ । दरिगह तेरी सांईयां , ना मरूम कोइ होइ ॥

meera.kk.10.m: Hari, look my way, just a little. I keep looking at you, and you do not look back; how hard your heart is! All my hope is in your glance; I have no other place.
meera.kk.10.r: Meera pada "Tanak Hari chitvau ji mori or"
roles: Shows all hope hanging on one glance.
meera.kk.10.sa: तनक हरि चितवौ जी मोरी ओर। हम चितवत तुम चितवत नाहीं मन के बड़े कठोर। मेरे आसा चितनि तुम्हरी और न दूजी ठौर।

meera.kk.11.m: Hari, you are the support of my life and breath. In all three worlds I have no shelter but you.
meera.kk.11.r: Meera pada "Hari mere jivan pran adhar"
roles: Shows the one named as shelter.
meera.kk.11.sa: हरि मेरे जीवन प्राण अधार। और आसरो नांही तुम बिन, तीनू लोक मंझार।।

meera.kk.12.m: O mind, touch Hari's feet: lovely, cool, soft as lotus, taking away the threefold fire.
meera.kk.12.sa: मन रे परसि हरि के चरन। सुभग सीतल कमल- कोमल त्रिविध - ज्वाला- हरन।

meera.kk.13.m: I have found the jewel-wealth of Ram's name. My true teacher gave me a priceless thing and in kindness made me his own. I found the savings of many lives and lost all the world's. Spending does not exhaust it, no thief can steal it; it grows day by day.
roles: Shows the joy of having found.
meera.kk.13.sa: पायो जी म्हें तो राम रतन धन पायो। वस्तु अमोलक दी म्हारे सतगुरू, किरपा कर अपनायो॥ जनम-जनम की पूँजी पाई, जग में सभी खोवायो। खरच न खूटै चोर न लूटै, दिन-दिन बढ़त सवायो॥

meera.kk.14.m: These two eyes will not listen to me; they flow like rivers in the monsoon.
meera.kk.14.r: Meera pada "Koi kahiyau re prabhu aavan ki"
roles: Depicts grief the will cannot manage.
meera.kk.14.sa: ए दोउ नैण कह्यो नहिं मानै, नदियां बहै जैसे सावन की।

meera.kk.2.m: Meera's pain will ease only when Saanwara becomes the healer.
roles: Names the healer as the one longed for.
meera.kk.2.sa: मीरा री प्रभु पीर मिटाँगा जब वैद साँवरो होय ॥

meera.kk.3.m: Friend, I am mad with love, and no one knows my pain. Only the wounded know what the wounded go through, only one who has been wounded.
meera.kk.3.r: Meera pada "Mero darad na jane koy"
meera.kk.3.sa: हे री मैं तो प्रेम-दिवानी मेरो दरद न जाणै कोय। घायल की गति घायल जाणै, जो कोई घायल होय।

meera.kk.4.m: Now I am in your shelter; keep me, treasure of kindness.
roles: Shows the act of taking refuge said aloud.
meera.kk.4.sa: अब मैं सरण तिहारी जी, मोहि राखौ कृपा निधान।

meera.kk.5.m: I watch the road, I sweep the path, standing there looking down the way.
meera.kk.5.sa: पन्थ निहारूँ डगर भुवारूँ, ऊभी मारग जोय।

meera.kk.6.m: You are called the virtuous, gracious master; in me are all the faults. (Come to my house, beloved.) I have no merit, I know no virtues; you are the one who forgives.
roles: Shows inviting him in without merit.
meera.kk.6.sa: तुम गुणवंत सुसाहिब कहिये मोमें औगुण सारा।। म्हारे घर आओ प्रीतम प्यारा।। मैं निगुणी कछु गुण नहिं जानूं तुम सा बगसणहारा।।

meera.kk.8.m: Please hear my plea. I am being swept away in the ocean of the world; pull me out, if you will.
meera.kk.8.r: Meera pada "Tum suno ji mharo arji"
roles: Shows the plea and its outcome both given to him.
meera.kk.8.sa: तुम सुणो जी म्हारो अरजी। भवसागर में बही जात हूँ काढ़ो तो थारी मरजी।

rahim.193.m: Rahim says: remembering is best of all, when it comes again and again. People who were separated meet again; know that this is why God takes birth.
rahim.193.sa: रहिमन सुधि सबते भली, लगै जो बारम्बार। बिछुरे मानुष फिरि मिलैं, यहै जानि अवतार॥

rahim.61.m: Rahim says: to the one who has been given body and mind, who has made a home in the heart, what joy or sorrow is left that needs telling?
roles: Shows no need to plead one's case.
rahim.61.sa: जेहिं रहीम तन-मन दियो, कियो हिए बिच भौन। तासों दुख-सुख कहन की, रही बात अब कौन॥

rahim.89.m: What does the blind world know of the divine sweetness of being low? Poor humble lowliness is good: it brings a friend like the Friend of the lowly.
roles: Cultivates humility that draws the Lord close.
rahim.89.sa: दिव्य दीनता के रसहिं, का जानै जग अन्धु। भली बिचारी दीनता, दीनबन्धु-से बन्धु॥

rahim.91.m: Rahim says: people laugh when they hear of your sorrow and do not keep you steady. Raghuvir listens to what you say, and having listened, acts. That is how he is.
roles: Shows taking sorrow to the Lord.
rahim.91.sa: दुख नर सुनि हाँसी करैं, धरैं रहीम न धीर। कही सुनैं सुनि-सुनि करैं, ऐसे वे रघुवीर॥

st.bh.ascetic_and_king.l: When the mind is content, nobody is richer than you.
st.bh.ascetic_and_king.s: An ascetic tells a king who ignores him that learning equals wealth, that contentment in bark equals contentment in silk, and that pride over a few towns is a fever.
st.bh.ascetic_and_king.t: Vairagyashatakam: Dialogue between the ascetic and the king

st.bh.dog_and_elephant.l: Keep your dignity without needing to win every fight.
st.bh.dog_and_elephant.s: Images of the lion and the elephant celebrate self-respect and inborn spirit. Some verses lean toward intolerance of insult, a warrior-king ideal.

st.bh.forced_laughter_before_fools.l: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.
st.bh.forced_laughter_before_fools.s: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.

st.bh.house_of_many_then_one.l: Time is passing while you're busy; notice it before it's gone.
st.bh.house_of_many_then_one.s: Time empties cities, houses and courts; the busy never notice it passing; parents and childhood friends become memories. The section ends with life as a play and death as the curtain.
st.bh.house_of_many_then_one.t: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time

st.bh.proud_man_asks_for_his_children.l: Keep your dignity; ask for help for others before you ever grovel for yourself.
st.bh.proud_man_asks_for_his_children.s: On the humiliation of begging favours from the rich: only hungry children could make a proud man ask. Contentment, not wealth, is real joy.
st.bh.proud_man_asks_for_his_children.t: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of begging and servility

st.bh.three_kinds_of_people.l: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.
st.bh.three_kinds_of_people.s: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
st.bh.three_kinds_of_people.t: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned

st.bh.wrinkles_but_craving_young.l: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.
st.bh.wrinkles_but_craving_young.s: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.

st.bhakti.sur_gajendra_calls_last.l: Fight with everything you have; when your strength runs out, call. Help comes running.
st.bhakti.sur_gajendra_calls_last.s: An elephant king is seized by a crocodile in a lake and struggles for a thousand years with all his strength and his herd. Only when his strength is gone does he call out to Hari, who leaves his mount behind and runs barefoot to free him. Surdas returns to the story again and again (vp.11, 21, 241, 256).
st.bhakti.sur_gajendra_calls_last.t: The elephant who finally called (as Surdas sings it)

sur.bgs.10.m: Stay well, mother Yashoda. In four or five days we two brothers will come. Since the day I was parted from you, no one has called me "Kanhaiya". I have not had breakfast in the morning, nor warm milk at evening.
roles: Shows the small daily cares of a mother are gone.
sur.bgs.10.sa: नीके रहियो जसुमति मैया। आवैंगे दिन चारि पाँच में हम हलधर दोउ भैया॥ जा दिन तें हम तुमतें बिछुरे काहु न कह्यो 'कन्हैया'। कबहूँ प्रात न कियो कलेवा, साँझ न पीन्हीं धैया॥

sur.bgs.315.m: Come and meet me just once, Madhav. Who knows when the breath may leave; let the heart's wish not remain.
roles: Shows fear that time will run out first.
sur.bgs.315.sa: बारक जाइयो मिलि माधौ। को जानै कब छूटि जायगो स्वाँस, रहै जिय साधौ॥

sur.bgs.316.m: Night and day our eyes keep raining. Ever since Shyam went away, it is always the rainy season for us.
sur.bgs.316.sa: निसिदिन बरसत नैन हमारे। सदा रहति पावस ऋतु हम पै जब तें स्याम सिधारे॥

sur.bgs.34.m: Surdas says: I cannot forget Mohan's face for a moment, sleeping or waking.
roles: Shows the absent one present in every waking and sleeping moment.
sur.bgs.34.sa: सूरदास मोहि निमिष न बिसरत मोहन सूरति सोवत जागत॥

sur.bgs.9.m: "Though Mathura has great splendour, nothing pleases me without you." Surdas says: meeting the people of Braj, his heart grows cool and calm.
roles: Everything is here and nothing pleases without them.
sur.bgs.9.sa: यद्यपि मथुरा बिभव बहुत है तुम बिनु कछु न सुहाय। सूरदास ब्रजबासी लोगनि भेंटत हृदय जुड़ाय॥

sur.vp.1.m: I bow to the lotus feet of Hari, by whose grace the lame cross mountains and the blind see everything; the deaf hear, the mute speak again, and the pauper walks with a royal canopy over his head. Surdas says: my master is full of compassion; again and again I bow at his feet.
roles: Shows bowing at the feet as the opening act.
sur.vp.1.sa: चरन-कमल बंदों हरि-राइ। जाकी कृपा पंगु गिरि लंघे, अंधे कों सब कछु दरसाइ ॥ बहिरौ सुने, गूँग पुनि बोले, रंक चले सिर छत्र धराइ | सूरदास स्वामी करुनामय, बार बार बंदों तिहि पाइ ॥

sur.vp.107.m: Now even those troubles are gone. Back then, whenever I remembered you in my heart, you met me right then. For the good of your poor servant you walked along beside me, and kept me through all of it as the eyelid keeps the eye.
roles: Gratitude for being kept through it cultivates gratitude.
sur.vp.107.sa: अब वे बिपदा हू न रहीं। मनसा करि सुमिरत हे जब-जब, मिलते तब-तबहीं ॥ अपने दीन दास के हित लगि, फिरते सँग-सँगहीं । लेते राखि पलक गोलक ज्यों, संतत तिन सबहीं ॥

sur.vp.11.m: I have never seen a friend like Hari. Remember him in a time of trouble, and at that very moment he comes and stands between you and it.
roles: Remembering him in the hard hour.
sur.vp.11.sa: हरि सो मीत न देख्यौ कोई । विपति-काल सुमिरत, तिहिं औसर आनि तिरीछो होई ॥

sur.vp.125.m: The chatak, gazing up, bears every hardship in hope of the rain cloud, yet asks no other water.
roles: Shows waiting that does not look elsewhere.
sur.vp.125.sa: चातक चितवन पारि । घन-आसा सब दुख सहै, (पै) अनत न जाँचे बारि ॥

sur.vp.14.m: Govind accepts everyone's love. In whatever spirit his people serve him, he knows the movement of the heart within.
roles: Serves in the way that is truly yours.
sur.vp.14.sa: गोबिंद प्रीति सबनि की मानत | जिहि जिहि भाइ करत जन सेवा, अंतर की गति जानत ॥

sur.vp.141.m: Great is the shelter of the name. When you come for refuge, the Lord never turns you out; he builds you forts of kindness.
roles: Names taking the shelter of the name.
sur.vp.141.sa: बड़ी है राम नाम की ओट | सरन गएँ प्रभु काढ़ि देत नहिं, करत कृपा के कोट ।

sur.vp.144.m: The joy that comes from singing of Gopal does not come from chanting or austerity, or bathing at ten million holy places.
sur.vp.144.sa: जो सुख होत गुपालहि गाए । सो सुख होत न जप-तप कीन्हें, कोटिक तीरथ न्हाएं ॥

sur.vp.153.m: Ram is the wealth of us who have nothing. No thief takes it, it never runs low, and it comes through in hard times.
sur.vp.153.sa: हमारे निर्धन के धन राम । चोर न लेत, घटत नहिं कबहूँ, आवत गाढ़े काम ॥

sur.vp.16.m: He, the water of whose feet Shiva bears on his head and which blesses the three worlds — that Lord, for the sake of the sons of Pandu, washed feet with his own hands.
roles: Service as the mark of greatness.
sur.vp.16.sa: जाको चरनोदक सिव सिर धरि, तीनि लोक हितकारी । सोइ प्रभु पांडु-सुतनि के कारन निज कर चरन पखारी ॥

sur.vp.167.m: Lord, do not weigh my good points and my faults.
roles: Shows trust placed in mercy, not merit.

sur.vp.170.m: Lord, you have done so much for me: you gave me a human body for remembering you, though I, a sinner, achieved nothing with it. In the terror of the womb, head down, even there you did not forget me.
roles: Counting what was given before one could ask.
sur.vp.170.sa: तुम प्रभु, मोसों बहुत करी | नर-देही दीनी सुमिरन को, मो पापी ते कछु न सरी ॥ गरभ-बास अति त्रास, अधोमुख, तहाँ न मेरी सुधि बिसरी।

sur.vp.173.m: Who wouldn't love a virtuous, pure servant? The Lord's greatness is this: that the lowly find shelter.
sur.vp.173.sa: सुकृती सुचि सेवक जन काहि न जिय भावै। प्रभु की प्रभुता यहै जु दीन सरन पावे॥

sur.vp.176.m: Do whatever it takes, kind to the lowly, so that your servant never lets go of your feet even for a moment, ocean of compassion, delight of devotees.
sur.vp.176.sa: सोइ कछु कीजे दीन-दयाल ! जातें जन छन चरन न छाँड़े, करुना-सागर, भक्त-रसाल

sur.vp.18.m: No one else feels the pain of his people. Whenever the lowly were in sorrow, every time, Balbir showed them kindness.
roles: Trust from the record of his mercy.
sur.vp.18.sa: और न काहुहि जन की पीर। जब जब दीन दुखी भयो, तब तब कृपा करी बलबीर॥

sur.vp.2.m: The Lord is the companion of exactly those who have no one: kind to the lowly, supremely compassionate, Hari who takes many forms for the good of his people.
roles: Shows leaning on the companion of the companionless.
sur.vp.2.sa: नाथ अनाथनि ही के संगी। दीनदयाल, परम करुनामय, जन-हित हरि बहु-रंगी ॥

sur.vp.211.m: Who does not honour their own? A child may do ten million wrongs, and the mother does not count them.
roles: Shows resting in being his own.
sur.vp.211.sa: अपुने को को न आदर देइ ? ज्यों बालक अपराध कोटि करे, मातु न माने तेइ ॥

sur.vp.215.m: Leaving your name aside, Lord of the world, tell me, what other strength do I have?
roles: Names the name as the only strength.
sur.vp.215.sa: तुम्हरी नाम तजि प्रभु जगदीसर, सु तो कहो मेरे और कहा बल ?

sur.vp.219.m: Now keep me in your shelter, Lord. By your grace the elders were sent; as I was being swept away, they caught my hand.
roles: Names the people who caught his hand as grace.
sur.vp.219.sa: अब मोहि सरन राखिये नाथ ! कृपा करी जो गुरुजन पठए, बह्यो जात गह्यो हाथ ॥

sur.vp.220.m: However you keep me, so I will live. You know all the joys and sorrows of your people; why should I say them aloud? Sometimes I get food, kind one, sometimes I go hungry; sometimes I ride a horse or a great elephant, sometimes I carry loads myself.
roles: Names feast and hunger taken alike.
sur.vp.220.sa: जैसे राखहु तैसे रहौं। जानत हौ दुख-सुख सब जन के, मुख करि कहा कहौं ॥ कबहुँक भोजन लहाों कृपानिधि, कबहुँक भूख सहोँ। कवहुँक चढ़ों तुरंग, महा गज, कबहुँक भार बहों ॥

sur.vp.229.m: Who will hear this matter of mine? I see no one capable but you. To whom shall I tell my pain, Banwari?
roles: Gives pain to the one hearer.
sur.vp.229.sa: कौन सुने यह बात हमारी | समरथ ओर न देखों तुम विनु, कासों विथा कहों बनवारी ॥

sur.vp.235.m: You are my way and my keeper; anywhere else I find only sorrow. Called yours, whose else could I be called now?
roles: Known as his and content to be.
sur.vp.235.sa: मेरी तो गति-पति तुम, अनतहिं दुख पाऊँ। हों कहाइ तेरों, अब कोन कौ कहाऊँ ॥

sur.vp.236.m: Good or bad, we are yours. Our shame and our honour are yours to carry. Hear my plea, my Lord.
roles: Shows handing over both shame and honour.
sur.vp.236.sa: जौ हम भले बुरे तो तेरे। तुम्हें हमारी लाज-बड़ाई, बिनती सुनि प्रभु मेरे ॥

sur.vp.245.m: Such is the Lord, master of those who have no one: kind to the lowly, brimming with love, knowing every heart from within.
roles: Names trust in the knower of hearts.
sur.vp.245.sa: ऐसे प्रभु अनाथ के स्वामी | दीनदयाल, प्रेम-परिंपूरन, सब घट अंतरजामी ॥

sur.vp.250.m: You have never once delayed. By nature easy to reach and won over by remembrance, you have always given your devotees what is undying.
sur.vp.250.sa: कबहूँ तुम नाहिन गहरु कियो | सदा सुभाव-सुलभ सुमिरन-बस, भक्तनि अमर दियौ ॥

sur.vp.256.m: Hari, you are the companion of those in a tight spot.

sur.vp.258.m: Pleased by a single tulsi leaf, the Lord gives everything.
sur.vp.258.sa: सरबस प्रभु रीझि देत तुलसी के पाता॥

sur.vp.270.m: Remember me, Lord of Braj. I have no one else in the world to set me right but you.
sur.vp.270.sa: मेरी सुधि लीजो हो, ब्रजराज । और नहीं जग मैं कोउ मेरो, तुमहि सुधारन काज़ ॥

sur.vp.271.m: My Lord, do not hold my faults in your mind. Your name is "the one who sees all alike"; live up to it and carry me across. One piece of iron is kept in the shrine for worship, another lies in a butcher's house; the touchstone knows no such difference, and turns both into pure gold.
roles: Asks to be carried across as one is.
sur.vp.271.sa: हमारे प्रभु, औगुन चित न धरो । समदरसी है नाम तुम्हारा, सोई पार करौ॥ इक लोहा पूजा में राखत, इक घर बधिक परो। सो दुबिधा पारस नहिं जानत, कंचन करत खरो॥

sur.vp.279.m: Fortune into trouble, trouble into fortune — that is the nature of the body's life. Trees flower, fruit and shed their leaves, each in its season.
sur.vp.279.sa: संपति बिपति, बिपति ते संपति, देह कौ यहै सुभाइ ॥ तरुवर फूले, फरे, पतझरे, अपने कालहि पाइ।

sur.vp.281.m: Not all days pass the same. Keep remembering and singing of Hari while the body is well.
sur.vp.281.sa: सबे दिन एके-से नहि जात। सुमिरन-भजन कियौ करि हरि कौ,जब लों तन-कुसलात॥

sur.vp.295.m: Gentle words, humility with everyone, and always remain joyful.
sur.vp.295.sa: कोमल बचन, दीनता सब सौं, सदा अनंदित रहिये ।

sur.vp.297.m: How could the Lord forget one who has come to him for refuge? He sent nourishment to the child in the mother's womb, then turned blood into milk.
roles: Trust from what was already given.
sur.vp.297.sa: जो प्रभु के सरनागत आवे। ताकों प्रभु क्यों करि बिसरावे ॥ मातु-उदर में रस पहुँचावत। बहुरि रुधिर तें छीर बनावत ॥

sur.vp.300.m: Where else will my mind find happiness? Like the bird on a ship at sea that flies off and comes back to the ship again.
sur.vp.300.sa: मेरो मन अनत कहाँ सुख पावे । जैसे उड़ि जहाज को पच्छी, फिरि जहाज पर आये ॥

sur.vp.301.m: Devotion to you is my very breath. If it were gone, how would your servant live? Like a leaf without water.
roles: Shows devotion as what keeps him alive.
sur.vp.301.sa: तुम्हारी भक्ति हमारे प्रान । छूटि गए केसे जन जीवत, ज्यों पानी बिनु पान ॥

sur.vp.32.m: Lord, trust in your word is true: the master who sustains the whole universe feeds and holds us.
sur.vp.32.sa: प्रभु तेरो बचन भरोसों साँचों। पोषन भरन विसंभर साहब,

sur.vp.37.m: The one whom Manmohan takes into his embrace — not a hair falls from his head, even if the whole world turns hostile.
roles: Shows fearlessness from belonging to him.
sur.vp.37.sa: जाकों मनमोहन अंग करे। ताकौ केस खसे नहिं सिर ते, जो जग बैर परे ॥

sur.vp.423.m: As a river that meets the sea never flows back again, so Sur's mind, given to the lotus-eyed one, does not wander elsewhere.
sur.vp.423.sa: जैसे सरिता मिले सिंधु को, बहुरि प्रवाह न आवे (हो)। ऐसे सूर कमल-लोचन तें, चित नहिं अनत डुलावै (हो) ॥

sur.vp.71.m: O mind, stay Govind's. … Sorrow, joy, fame, fortune — whatever falls to you, take it as it comes.
roles: Shows sorrow and joy taken alike.
sur.vp.71.sa: रे मन, गोबिंद के है रहिये। … दुख, सुख, कीरति, भाग आपने आइ परे सो गहिये।

sur.vp.76.m: Make Nandnandan the master of the house, and live in it yourself as his servant.
roles: Shows service in running the home as service.
sur.vp.76.sa: नंदनंदन करि घर कौ ठाकुर, आपुन है रह चेरो ॥

surya_gita.6.60.m: Lord, now teach us how to restrain this mind, restless as the wind, so that we can remember you for lasting peace.
roles: A mind that will not stay.
surya_gita.6.60.sa: प्रभो! तथोपदेष्टव्यं वातवच्चपलं मन: यथा निगृह्य शक्ष्यामस्त्वां स्मर्तुं चिरशान्तये ॥

surya_gita.6.64.m: The love one has for a spouse and friends, the reverent trust one has for parents: when seekers turn that toward me, it is called devotion.
roles: Shows devotion as a love one already knows how to feel.
surya_gita.6.64.sa: स्त्रीमित्रादिषु सः प्रेमा श्रद्धा स जनकादिषु । मय्येव साधकानां स भक्तिरित्यभिधीयते ॥

tulsi_dv.100.m: Everyone became an obstacle to everyone; no one became a helper. Tulsi says: whatever good comes will come from the kind Ram.
tulsi_dv.100.sa: बाधक सब सब के भए साधक भए न कोइ। तुलसी राम कृपालु तें भलो होइ सो होइ॥

tulsi_dv.101.m: A child plays with a snake and reaches for the fire; as a father and mother keep that child safe, Tulsi says, so Sita and Ram keep us.
roles: Care that works before one asks.
tulsi_dv.101.sa: खेलत बालक ब्याल सँग मेलत पावक हाथ। तुलसी सिसु पितु मातु ज्यो राखत सिय रघुनाथ॥

tulsi_dv.109.m: I begged for scraps from house to house; later kings bowed at my feet. The Tulsi who was then without Ram now has Ram's help.
tulsi_dv.109.sa: घर घर मागे टूक पुनि भूपति पूजे पाय। जे तुलसी तब राम बिनु ते अब राम सहाय॥

tulsi_dv.143.m: Tulsidas, remember the feet that freed the woman turned to stone from her curse. Let your worry go: the trouble will pass and the heart's hope will be met.
roles: Shows trust built on what those feet have done.
tulsi_dv.143.sa: सिला साप मोचन चरन सुमिरहु तुलसीदास । तजहु सोच संकट मिटिहिं पूजहि मनकी आस॥

tulsi_dv.152.m: A straight mind, straight words, straight deeds in everything: Tulsi says, all this straightness is born of love for Raghubar.
roles: Love for Raghuvar as what gives birth to them.
tulsi_dv.152.sa: सूधे मन सूधे बचन सूधी सब करतूति। तुलसी सूधी सकल बिधि रघुबर प्रेम प्रसूति॥

tulsi_dv.256.m: Making a home, the true home is lost; leaving home, home is lost too. Tulsi says: between home and forest, settle in the city of Ram's love.
roles: Shows living in Ram's love wherever one is.
tulsi_dv.256.sa: घर कोन्हें घर जात है घर छाँड़े घर जाइ। तुलसी घर बन बीचहीं राम प्रेम पुर छाइ॥

tulsi_dv.278.m: Whether the cloud rains on time, or stays indifferent my whole life, Tulsi says: this chataka heart still hopes in you.
roles: Shows hope that does not depend on being answered.
tulsi_dv.278.sa: जौ घन बरषे समय सिर जौँ भरि जनम उदास। तुलसी या चित चातकहि तऊ तिहारी आस॥

tulsi_dv.282.m: One trust, one strength, one hope and faith: for the chataka Tulsidas, the one dark cloud, Ram, is his friend.
tulsi_dv.282.sa: एक भरोसो एक बल एक आस बिस्वास । एक राम घन स्याम हित चातक तुलसीदास॥

tulsi_dv.405.m: When the one you trusted enough to sleep with your head in their lap turns on you, Tulsi says, the Lord of the world is your guardian.
roles: Shows God as guard where trust was broken.
tulsi_dv.405.sa: जासु भरोसें सोइऐे राखि गोद में सीस। तुलसी तासु कुचाल तें रखवारो जगदीस॥

tulsi_dv.424.m: Better to step away, better to shield yourself; better not to strike a wound. Tulsi says: over everyone's head stands Raghurao, the guardian.
roles: Shows a guardian over everyone's head.
tulsi_dv.424.sa: भागें भल ओड़ेहुँ भलो भलो न घालें घाउ। तुलसी सब के सीस पर रखवारो रघुराउ॥

tulsi_dv.528.m: The servant who knows his own duty is greater than the master: Ram had to build a bridge to cross the ocean; Hanuman simply leapt across.
roles: Service done with full knowledge of one's duty.
tulsi_dv.528.sa: साहब तें सेवक बड़ो जो निज धरम सुजान। राम बाँधि उतरे उदधि लाँघि गए हनुमान॥

tulsi_dv.84.m: Lord of Kosala, whatever I am, I am yours alone; and so Tulsi is well in all three worlds and all three times.
tulsi_dv.84.sa: जैसो तैसो रावरो केवल कोसलपाल। तौ तुलसी को है भलो तिहूँ लोक तिहुँ काल॥

tulsi_dv.85.m: People call Tulsi a treasury of faults, but he has one virtue: a good trust in you, Ram, which is fit to please you.
roles: Names trust as his single qualification.
tulsi_dv.85.sa: है तुलसी कें एक गुन अवगुन निधि कहैं लोग। भलो भरोसो रावरो राम रीझिले जोग॥

tulsi_dv.95.m: Hold Ram in awe; give Ram your closeness, love and trust. Tulsi says: once you belong to Ram without conditions, even losing is winning.
roles: Shows defeat and victory losing their difference.
tulsi_dv.95.sa: रामहि डरु करू राम सों ममता प्रीति प्रतीति। तुलसी निरुपधि राम को भएँ हारेहूँ जीति॥

tulsi_dv.96.m: Tulsi, tell the kind Ram all of it, your good points and your faults. Your misery will grow thin and your contentment will grow full.
tulsi_dv.96.sa: तुलसी राम कृपालु सों कहि सुनाउ गुन दोष। होय दूबरी दीनता परम पीन संतोष॥

tulsi_gv.2.52.m: The mother gazes at his little bow and arrows. Again and again she presses the Lord's small, lovely shoes to her heart and eyes. Sometimes, as before, she goes to wake him with tender words: "Get up, my child, your mother adores your face; your brothers and friends are all at the door."
roles: Shows she presses his small shoes to her heart and eyes.
tulsi_gv.2.52.sa: जननी निरखति बान-धनुहियाँ। बार-बार उर नैननि लावति प्रभुजूकी ललित पनहियाँ॥ कबहुँ प्रथम ज्यों जाइ जगावति कहि प्रिय बचन सँवारे। उठहु तात! बलि मातु बदनपर, अनुज-सखा सब द्वारे॥

tulsi_gv.5.42.m: Whoever goes to Ram for refuge is well: rich or poor, great or small, wise or foolish, weak or very strong. The lame, the blind, those without virtue or provision, who do not get water even when they ask: whoever was born in the world and walked Ram's royal road was looked after well.
tulsi_gv.5.42.sa: गये राम सरन सबकौ भलो। गनी-गरीब, बड़ो-छोटो, बुध-मूढु, हीनबल-अतिबलो॥ १ ॥ पंगु-अंध, निरगुनी-निसंबल, जो न लहै जाचे जलो। सो निबह्यो नीके, जो जनमि जग राम-राजमारग चलो॥

tulsi_gv.5.44.m: The Lord knows the joys and sorrows of his servants, so I have not told mine. Look at me with eyes full of kindness; then I'll know you have made me your own.
roles: Shows him asking only to be looked at with compassion.
tulsi_gv.5.44.sa: जानत प्रभु दुख-सुख दासनिको, तातें कहि न सुनायो। करि करुना भरि नयन बिलोकहु, तब जानौं अपनायो॥

tulsi_gv.5.45.m: Lacking in every way, poor, very slow-witted, with no place anywhere: if such a one comes for refuge, I care for him and never abandon him; the great sages know this. Again and again I raise my arm and say it, let the whole assembly believe me: no one is as dear to me as my servant; let false love be swept away.
tulsi_gv.5.45.sa: सब बिधि हीन-दीन, अति जड़मति जाको कतहुँ न ठाउँ। आयो सरन भजौं, न तजौँ तिहि, यह जानत रिपिराठ॥ … पुनि पुनि भुजा उठाइ कहत हौं, सकल सभा पतिआउ। नहि कोऊ प्रिय मोहि दास सम, कपट-प्रीति बहि जाउ॥

tulsi_hb.10.m: A body hard as a thunderbolt, a roar in battle, yet a mind full of compassion, righteous and steady. Terrible to the wicked, protector of the good: remembering him takes away Tulsi's pain. Giver of joy to Sita, darling of Raghunayak, the brave son of the wind is the helper of servants.
roles: Shows the protector of the good and helper of servants.
tulsi_hb.10.sa: कुलिस-कठोरतनु जोरपै रोर रन, करुना-कलित मन धारमिक धीरको॥ दुर्जजको कालसो कराल पाल सज्जनको, सुमरि हरनहार तुलसीकी पीरको। सीय-सुखदायक दुलारो रघुनायको, सेवक सहायक है साहसी समीरको॥

tulsi_hb.13.m: The kind sages and perfected ones will care for him like a child, in whose heart Hanuman's war-cry rings with joy.
roles: One is looked after like a child.
tulsi_hb.13.sa: बालक-ज्यों पालिहें कृपालु मुनि सिद्ध ताको, जाके हिये हुलसति हाँक हनुमानकी॥

tulsi_hb.17.m: Tulsi says: all troubles and worries tear apart like spider webs when your name is taken.
tulsi_hb.17.sa: संकट सोच सबै तुलसी लिये नाम फटै मकरीके-से जाले।

tulsi_hb.22.m: Messenger of Ram, wishing tree for Ram's servants: for a poor, weak one like me, you are the pillow I lean on.
tulsi_hb.22.sa: रामके गुलामनिको कामतरु रामदूत, मोसे दीन दूबरेको तकिया तिहारिये॥

tulsi_hb.29.m: A beggar going house to house for scraps: the kind protector of those who bow called me and raised me like his own child. Brave son of Anjani, you took care of me; do not forget your own, I trust in you too.
roles: Shows him remembering who raised him.
tulsi_hb.29.sa: टूकनिको घर-घर डोलत कंगाल बोलि, बाल ज्यों कृपाल नतपाल पालि पोसो है। कोन्ही है संभार सार अंजनीकुमार बीर, आपनो बिसारिं न मेरेहू भरोसो है॥

tulsi_hb.30.m: I tried many medicines, charms and remedies, prayed to the gods; it only got worse. Tulsi is your servant; you said 'you are mine', messenger of Ram. Your delay hurts me more than the pain.
roles: Names being told you are mine and help not coming.
tulsi_hb.30.sa: औषध अनेक जंंत्र-मंत्र-टोटकादि किये, बदि भये देवता मनाये अधिकाति है॥ … चेरो तेरो तुलसी तू मेरो कह्यो रामदूत, ढील तेरी बीर मोहि पीरतें पिराति है॥

tulsi_hb.33.m: Lord of the monkeys, stroke Tulsi's head with your hand. With a protector like you, let your servant not be seen in pain.
roles: Shows him asking his protector for one gentle act.
tulsi_hb.33.sa: तुलसीके माथेपर हाथ फेरो कीसनाथ, देखिये न दास दुखी तोसे कनिगरके॥

tulsi_hb.34.m: You are the water and I the fish; you are the mother and I the baby. So do not delay, for you are my only support. Knowing the child is in distress, protect him; recognise the love, and stroke Tulsi's aching arm with your long tail.
roles: Shows you are my only support.
tulsi_hb.34.sa: अंबु तू हौं अंबुचर, अंब तू हौं डिंभ, सो न, बूझिये बिलंब अवलंब मेरे तेरिये। बालक बिकल जानि पाहि प्रेम पहिचानि, तुलसीकी बाह पर लामीलूम फेरिये॥

tulsi_hb.40.m: Even while I did bad things, you took me as your own; son of Anjani, you cleansed me and made me fit for Ram's hand.
roles: Shows the one credits the one who cleaned him.
tulsi_hb.40.sa: खोटे-खोटे आचरन आचरत अपनायो, अंजनीकुमार सोध्यो रामपानि पाक हौं।

tulsi_kv.7.11.m: For the hurting, the poor and those with no one, Raghunath makes shade with his own hand.
tulsi_kv.7.11.sa: आरत, दीन, अनाथनको रघुनाथु करैं निज हाथकी छाहें॥

tulsi_kv.7.128.m: Sword drawn, no mercy anywhere, the boy did not run on seeing his terrible father. 'Where is Ram?' 'Everywhere.' 'In this pillar?' 'Yes.' Hearing that cry, the man-lion awoke.
roles: Answers plainly under a raised sword.
tulsi_kv.7.128.sa: काढ़ि कृपान, कृपा न कहूँ, पितु काल कराल बिलोकि न भागे। “राम कहाँ ?' “सब ठाउँ हें', 'खंभमें ?' ' हा' सुनि हाँक नृकेहरि जागे॥

scene.s: Prahlad, his father's sword raised over him.

tulsi_kv.7.129.m: Kind Ram, protector of the hurting: wherever anyone remembers him, there he stands.
tulsi_kv.7.129.sa: आरतपाल कृपाल जो रामु जेहीं सुमिरे तेहिको तहँ ठाढ़े।

tulsi_kv.7.182.m: Greater than the Ram who dwells within is the Ram outside, who comes when his name is called: he runs the way a cow runs, milk flowing, when she hears her calf's cry.
tulsi_kv.7.182.sa: अंतरजामिहुतें बड़े बाहेरजामि हैं राम, जे नाम लियेतें। धावत धेनु पेन्हाइ लवाई ज्यों बालक-बोलनि कान कियेतें॥

tulsi_kv.7.36.m: Ram is my mother, father, teacher, brother, companion, friend, son, master and beloved. I swear by Ram, my trust is in Ram; I am coloured by Ram, and my heart is taken by no one else.
roles: Shows being dyed in Ram and drawn to no one else.
tulsi_kv.7.36.sa: रामु हैं मातु, पिता, गुरु, बंधु, औ संगी, सखा, सुतु, स्वामि, सनेही। रामको सौंह, भरोसो है रामको, राम रंँग्यो, रुचि राच्यो न केही॥

tulsi_kv.7.37.m: My mind is with Ram, my goal is with Ram, my love is for Ram, Ram is my strength. I don't speak for everyone; in Tulsi's view, this much is the fruit of living in the world.
roles: Shows not imposing his view on others.
tulsi_kv.7.37.sa: मति रामहि सों, गति रामहि सों, रति रामसों, रामहि को बलु है। सबकी न कहै, तुलसीके मतें इतनो जग जीवनको फलु है॥

tulsi_kv.7.48.m: Prahlad felt not the least despair, because of the strength of the man-lion. Whom should Tulsi fear? If Ram protects, who can kill?
tulsi_kv.7.48.sa: नेकु बिषादु नहीं प्रहलादहि कारन केहरिके बल हो रे। कौनकी त्रास करै तुलसी जो पै राखिहै राम, तौ मारिहै को रे॥

tulsi_kv.7.50.m: Where there are a million dangers, Tulsi, and no son, mother, father, friend or kin is near, kind Ram will protect you there, he who has a servant like Hanuman. In heaven, the underworld or on earth, Raghunayak is my one helper.
roles: Shows one helper in every world.
tulsi_kv.7.50.sa: संकट कोटि जहाँ 'तुलसी', सुत, मातु, पिता, हित, बंधु न नेरे॥ राखिहैँ रामु कृपालु तहाँ, हनुमानु-से सेवक हैं जेहि केरे। नाक, रसातल, भूतलमें रघुनायकु एकु सहायकु मेरे॥

tulsi_kv.7.53.m: Where there is no kind master, no friend beside you, no wife, son, brother, father or mother, there is one who forgives every fault of body, word and mind, without holding back. Tulsi, at that time who but the kind one can calm the terrible pain? Where everything is crisis and the worry seems impossible, there my master Ram keeps me.
roles: Depicts every crisis at once and a worry with no solution.
tulsi_kv.7.53.sa: जहाँ हित स्वामि, न संग सखा, बनिता, सुत, बंधु, न बापु, न मैया। काय-गिरा-मनके जनके अपराध सबै छलु छाडि छमैया॥ तुलसी! तेहि काल कृपाल बिना दूजो कौन है दारुन दुःख दमैया॥ जहाँ सब संकट, दुर्घट सोचु, तहाँ मेरो साहेबु राखे रमैया॥

tulsi_kv.7.57.m: My mother and father brought me into the world and left me; fate wrote nothing good on my forehead. Lowly, scorned, timid, I hungered like a dog for scraps. Then Tulsi heard of Ram's nature and, just once, showed the Lord his empty stomach. Such a master is Raghunath that he held nothing back, in this world or the next.
roles: Shows he showed his empty stomach just once.
tulsi_kv.7.57.sa: मातु-पिताँ जग जाइ तज्यो बिधिहूँ न लिखी कछु भाल भलाई। नीच, निरादरभाजन, कादर, कूकर-टूकन लागि ललाई॥ रामु-सुभाउ सुन्यो तुलसीं प्रभुसों कह्यो बारक पेटु खलाई। स्वारथको परमारथको रघुनाथु सो साहेबु, खोरि न लाई॥

tulsi_kv.7.67.m: A high mind, high tastes, and very low luck; no good at worldly ways, a stubborn talker. Selfish gain was out of reach, never mind higher goals; the belly's demands are hard on every living being. No job, no mine, no farm, no trade, no begging; the fool knows no craft or skill. Tulsi's game was saved by Ram's name alone.
roles: Shows the name as the one stake he had.
tulsi_kv.7.67.sa: उँचो मनु, ऊँची रुचि, भागु नीचो निपट ही, लोकरीति-लायक न, लंगर लबारु है। स्वारथु अगमु, परमारथकी कहा चली, पेटकी कठिन जगु जीवको जबारु है॥ चाकरी न आकरी, न खेती, न बनिज-भीरख, जानत न कूर कछु किसब कबारु है। तुलसीकी बाजी राखी रामहीकें नाम,

tulsi_kv.7.7.m: Even when his people commit faults beyond measure, he does not take them into his heart.
roles: Shows trust in a memory that does not keep score.
tulsi_kv.7.7.sa: अपराध अगाध भएँ जनते, अपने उर आनत नाहिन जू।

tulsi_kv.7.73.m: Born into a family of beggars, my birth brought my parents only grief. From childhood I wandered door to door, wailing with want, thinking four grains of chickpea were the four great goals of life. Now that same Tulsi is the trusted servant of a mighty master, and even the stars' accountant is amazed. Ram, is your name clever or mad, that it makes one lighter than a straw heavier than a mountain?
roles: Gives amazement at what the name did.
tulsi_kv.7.73.sa: जायो कुल मंगन, बधावनो बजायो, सुनि भयो परितापु पापु जननी-जनकको। बारेतें ललात-बिललात द्वार-द्वार दीन, जानत हो चारि फल चारि ही चनकको॥ तुलसी सो साहेब समर्थको सुसेवकु है, सुनत सिहात सोचु बिधिहू गनकको। नामु राम! रावरो सयानो किधौं बावरो, जो करत गिरीतें गरु तृनतें तनकको॥

tulsi_vp.101.m: Where would I go, leaving your feet? Whose name in the world is "the one who lifts the fallen"? To whom are the lowliest so very dear?
roles: Shows he stays at these feet.
tulsi_vp.101.sa: जाउँ कहाँ तजि चरन तुम्हारे। काको नाम पतित-पावन जग, केहि अति दीन पियारे॥

tulsi_vp.102.m: Hari, you have been very kind: out of grace you gave me this body, home of every practice, which even the gods find hard to get. Tulsidas says: the rope of delusion that binds this soul, only the one who tied it can untie.
tulsi_vp.102.sa: हरि! तुम बहुत अनुग्रह कीन्हों। साधन-धाम विबुध दुरलभ तनु, मोहि कृपा करि दीन्हों॥ … तुलसिदास येहि जीव मोह-रजु, जेहि बाँध्यो सोइ छोरै॥

tulsi_vp.103.m: This is my prayer, Raghubir, master: take away every other hope, trust and reliance, and the dullness of this soul. Wherever my crooked karma drags me by force, there do not leave off your care even for a moment, as the tortoise keeps watch over its eggs.
roles: Shows every other hope and trust given up.
tulsi_vp.103.sa: यह बिनती रघुबीर गुसाई। और आस-बिस्वास-भरोसो, हरो जीव-जड़ताई॥ … कुटिल करम लै जाहि मोहि जहँ जहँ अपनी बरिआई। तहँँ तहँ जनि छिन छोह छाँड़ियो, कमठ-अंडकी नाई॥

tulsi_vp.105.m: Till now it has been wasted; from now it will not be. By Ram's grace the long night is over. Now that I am awake, I will not spread the bed of sleep again.
tulsi_vp.105.sa: अबलों नसानी, अब न नसैहौं। राम-कृपा भव-निसा सिरानी, जागे फिरि न डसैहौं॥
